==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR ARJUNSINGH B CHAUHAN(11510) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR. AJENKUMAR A PATEL(17415) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR LB DABHI APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIKHIL S. KARIEL  Date : 05/01/2026

ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocate Mr. Arjunsingh B. Chauhan appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr.L.B.Dabhi appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.
2. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State.

3. The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being I-C.R. No.59 Manojbhai Bhagubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124428631/
1 of 2014 registered with Ichhapore Police Station, Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 114 of Indian Penal Code.
4.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that since the charge-sheet is filed no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.

It is further contended that the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/27555/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant as coming out from the charge- sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.

Following aspects are considered:
(i) While the FIR had been registered in the year 2014, it would appear that other co-accused had approached this Court by preferring petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. and whereas learned coordinate Bench of this Court having protected the co-accused the investigation had not proceeded and

whereas later on upon the said application being dismissed, the name of the present applicant appearing as accused based upon the statement of co-accused who had been protected;
(ii) the fact of co-accused having similar role, having been released by this Court,
(iii) the fact of there being an antecedent of the present applicant being involved in similar offence and the applicant having been considered for regular bail at the relevant point of time, that is to state that there are two FIRs filed against the co-accused in the year 2014 and whereas the applicant was named in one of the FIRs and present applicant having been considered for release by learned Sessions Court,
and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/27555/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined (iv) the co-accused has been considered for regular bail by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 09.12.2025 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.25816 of 2025.
This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.

sentences.text:
In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail,
prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present application is allowed.
9. The Authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Court concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
10. Bail bond to be executed before the lower court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.

11. At the stage of trial, the trial court shall not be influenced by any observations of this Court which are of preliminary nature made at this stage, only for the purpose of considering the application of the applicant for being released on regular bail.
12. The application is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(NIKHIL S. KARIEL,J) MISHRA AMIT V.
